could_not_do: THE THREE PLAYED GATES DID NOT RUN AND CANNOT RUN FROM A SUBAGENT. RI-UIX06 §G (six fresh Bootstrap judges on six --blank-world screens), RI-UIX07 §G/V11, and RI-UIX08 §G. `create_session` is approval-gated and CLAUDE.md rule 0 forbids me touching it; rule 0e places this squarely with the orchestrator. Each is scored 0 fail-closed within its item rather than omitted, and each caps its item. RI-UIX07 is the sharpest case: it is at 10/11 on the count and its own 6 rung NAMES V11 pass as a condition, so the count reaching the rung cannot buy it.

I BROKE MY OWN INSTRUMENT THREE TIMES AND CAUGHT ALL THREE, AND THEY ARE HERE RATHER THAN IN THE VERDICT AS FINDINGS. (1) `getUIState().focus` is `this.focus[this.mode]` — the ACTIVE screen's focus, FLAT — and I read `focus.journal` first, so every journal check returned `view: null` and would have read as a dead screen. Caught on the first run because JX0 (a check whose only job is to prove the trap's own door still opens) went red. (2) My refused-row leg matched `/bow/i` and landed on a 'Mud-slip bowl', then PASSED on a toast left over from the previous leg's successful equip — a false pass, which is worse than a false fail. Now selected by `meta.item_id === 'hist-sap-bow'` with `uiToast(null)` called immediately before the press. (3) `t4-r3-density.mjs` compared `d2()`'s RETURN OBJECT against the float 0.15, so my first density run reported `hard_fails: []` on four screens that all hard-fail — the exact shape of the defect this piece is failing on, in my own tool. All three are in the verdict's `method_deviations`.

TWO CHECKS IN MY FULL RUN MEASURED THE PROBE'S OWN HISTORY AND I THREW THEM AWAY RATHER THAN REPORT THEM. TS1/TS2 read `focus.rowIdx 43` — the LAST row of a 44-item carried list, left there by the equip legs — where a downward drag correctly cannot move, and reported a dead stick on a build whose stick works. The IC leg's row selector walked off the end of the list and pressed confirm on a `misc` bowl, which `_confirm()` queues nothing for, so it measured a press the UI never accepted and called it a dead commitment. Both are re-run in isolation with a new `--legs` filter and committed as separate artifacts with their own logs; the probe now asserts `TS0` (the list is at row 0) before it measures the stick, and selects the in-combat row by item id.

RI-UIX03 §B-§E ARE CARRIED FROM ROUND 2, NOT RE-RUN. What makes that defensible rather than lazy is a repo read taken in the same turn as the claim: `git diff --stat 398bd592..a711f451 -- game/data/` is EMPTY, so not one byte of the item data those five rows read has moved since the builder's own baseline. It is still the second-weakest claim in the verdict and I name it as such: if a sibling changed how a row is DRAWN without changing its data, my 8/13 is stale in a direction I cannot see. RI-UIX06 AD2/AD3/AD6 and RI-UIX07 V1-V6 are carried on the same footing; AD1 and V7/V8/V9 I re-measured.

RI-UIX06's FIDELITY SIDE IS UNCAPTURED FOR THE THIRD ROUND and AD4 is fail-closed on a measurement nobody has taken for the third round. I scored the ART side with its scope written on it rather than fail-closing FIDELITY to 0 and setting the piece min to 0 for a third round, because a 0 that says nothing about the build is worse than a number with its scope on it. The honest sentence is in the verdict: the item's ship gate `min(ART, FIDELITY) >= 6` is NOT SATISFIED AND CANNOT BE EVALUATED.

RI-UIX01 §D IS UNMEASURED FOR THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE ROUND AND I DID NOT MEASURE IT EITHER. I excluded it from the aggregate with its reason rather than scoring it, and I say plainly in the verdict that it should be its own piece: its six checks are about the stamina bar's correctness UNDER COMBAT, and its comparison method wants a `ui-combat` viewpoint set of eight poses that does not exist in `tools/harness/viewpoints.json` plus a combat trace with `--ui-visible`. Nothing about it is a screens-piece measurement, which is exactly why three critics in a row have deferred it for the same honest reason. Creating that piece is dispatch, not critique, so I recommended it and did not do it.

RI-UIX03 C4 (that crossing the encumbrance threshold changes roll distance and stamina cost) was not run — third round. `tools/harness/prg-encumbrance.mjs` exists and would settle it in one run. RI-UIX07 E-T5's deletion arm (a worktree with `game/src/ui/hud-world.js` removed) and V10's pixel half (the `ui-world` viewpoint sweep, which still does not exist) were not run. RI-UIX07 W6 (breath) has still never been observed drawn because nobody has submerged the body.

I DID NOT RUN A DELETE-THE-FIX ARM MYSELF. The builder ran one, in a real `git worktree` at `398bd592` with `tools/node_modules` symlinked per HAZARDS 7, and got 8/13 on the same probe that gives 12/13 on the fixed tree. I re-ran the FIXED arm with that same probe, byte-identical, and got the opposite result to the control — which is the half a critic is allowed to own. A critic re-running the builder's own control arm would be re-running the builder's evidence.

I PROCEEDED PAST NO CONTENTION WAIT. Every browser run in this piece was launched behind a `node tools/contention.mjs` GO, checked in the same shell invocation before the launch. Six browser sessions in total; peak concurrency two, against a ceiling of six. All browsers are dead at the end of this piece and every background waiter I armed has completed or been stopped by id.

what_i_found.the_arbitration_question_i_refused_to_se: RI-UIX03 P7 states the equip commitment UNCONDITIONALLY while its own comparison method measures it CONDITIONALLY ('during combat'), and round 3 set the commitment to 0 frames out of combat. CRITIC-DOCTRINE §7.4 forbids me inventing a ruling and §2.4 forbids me deferring to the builder's, so I stated both sides in `arbitration_questions` and scored M-P5 on the item's own comparison method, which measures a fight. IT IS NOT A FREE PASS AND I SAID SO: if P7 is read as unconditional, M-P5's hard fail ('instant equip swap') fires and RI-UIX03 drops from 3 to 2. The piece score does not move either way, which is why this is a question for the dimension owner rather than a finding.

bar_sufficiency_1_3: I checked whether these items can express what this piece needs to be good at, and they can — recorded even though the answer is yes, because its absence is indistinguishable from never having asked. The one candidate hole is the axis repeat: a list you can walk one press at a time is 'operable' under RI-UIX10 O1 and no item asks whether walking it is BEARABLE (a 40-frame held touch drag moves one row, 4 -> 5; a 40-frame held KeyS moves one row, 5 -> 6; the 44-item carried list therefore costs 43 presses). Ids checked before deciding: RI-UIX01, RI-UIX02, RI-UIX03, RI-UIX04, RI-UIX05, RI-UIX06, RI-UIX07, RI-UIX08, RI-UIX09, RI-UIX10, RI-JRN02, RI-JRN03, RI-JRN04, RI-JRN09, RI-CAM02. I did NOT extend the bar, for two reasons: RI-JRN03 KB2 already legislates key auto-repeat in the OPPOSITE direction ('every handler checks event.repeat and ignores repeats'), so a new row demanding repeat would collide with an existing one rather than fill a hole, and §1.3 lets me only add and never weaken; and it is not what caps this piece. Two of the seven items I was handed were written by the two previous critics under this same rule, and a third would have been a reflex rather than a finding. I DID file one corpus bug rather than absorb it into a score: RI-UIX10's ladder tops out at 8 with no 9 or 10 rung, so as written it cannot express 'beats the reference', which SCORING.md §0 requires at ship. It is in that item's why_not_ten.
